children: Copper prices rise above the $14,700-a-metric-ton mark, supported by a tight supply outlook and a rebound in tech stocks. "With the dollar having had little influence on recent price action, we see the near-term path for copper as increasingly momentum-led," analysts at Sucden Financial say. The market could test the $14,750 a ton area again, a level that may offer fresh resistance following the earlier reversal, according to the firm. A sustained move above it would signal stronger upward momentum, while renewed selling pressure could prompt traders to lock in gains after the recent rebound. In early European trading, three-month copper futures on the LME rise 0.5% to $14,743 a ton. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
